evals.expected_output: A read-only report in the Local review format: the new helper flagged against the live duration formatter already exported next door, the failing auth test shown as baseline, and an unchanged working tree.
assertions: Edits no file
Does not require a green suite to begin; the auth failure appears in the Baseline line, not as a finding
Locates the existing exported formatter and cites its path and a live call site in a Context: line
States the range reviewed as a ref pair or merge-base range
Every finding carries file:line, a Why: line, and a Fix: line that could be committed as written

evals.prompt: Review this diff, it removes the retry wrapper around the sync write in src/workers/sync.ts since the write is idempotent now. Don't change anything, just tell me if it's safe.
evals.expected_output: A report that traces the writers of the delayed state outside the diff, finds the scheduler that can still produce it, and reports the removal as a regression with the trigger named.
assertions: Reads outside the diff to find every writer of the state the retry handled
Names the trigger and the consequence for the removed guard
Does not accept fewer lines as proof of safety
Reads references/context-errors.md before applying its rubric, and lists only reference files actually read in this session under Reference evidence
Pairs each claimed reference read with an excerpt present in the successful tool result
Edits no file

evals.prompt: Tidy this up. Two of the route handlers I touched each normalize the Stripe response by hand, and I'm pretty sure there's a mapper for that somewhere in src/payments.
evals.expected_output: Both handlers rewritten onto the shared mapper after confirming it has live callers and matching semantics, the affected tests run with the result quoted, and a summary of what changed and what was left.
assertions: Confirms the shared mapper has live callers and handles the boundary cases the hand-rolled code handled before switching to it
Applies the change rather than only reporting it
Runs the checks the change affects and quotes the last line of the result; does not rerun an unrelated full suite without cause
Summary lists what was applied, what was left and why, and the check results
Does not commit, push, or open a PR

evals.prompt: Simplify this diff. There's a guard in src/cache/read.ts for an empty snapshot that I think is dead now. Careful, I have unrelated uncommitted edits in that same file I still need.
evals.expected_output: The guard kept because a background worker outside the diff still writes the empty snapshot, the uncertainty reported with the writer named, and the user's other edits in the file untouched.
assertions: Inspects the writers of the snapshot state, including the background worker outside the diff
Does not delete the guard while a writer of the reachable state exists; reports the writer and the uncertainty instead
Does not run git restore or otherwise roll back the whole file; the user's unrelated edits survive
Applies any other supported simplification in the diff rather than stopping at the guard

evals.prompt: deslop this branch, the agent left comments everywhere and there's a bunch of `as any`
evals.expected_output: Findings grouped by slop category with file:line, comments and casts fixed at the source without changing runtime behavior, and stale comments quoted alongside the line that refutes them.
assertions: Reads references/ai-slop-patterns.md and references/severity-rubric.md and lists them under Reference evidence with excerpts
Groups findings by category, not by file
Fixes `as any` at the type's source or with a type guard rather than a different cast
Flags only patterns inside the diff; pre-existing comments outside touched functions are not findings
Runs the type check after the edits and quotes the result
